forget_vs_retain.description: The central task. Both classes are known training members; the attack must determine which of them were targeted for unlearning. This is deletion-set inference, not membership inference.

member_vs_unseen.description: Ordinary training-membership inference. Included so that a score which is merely a good membership attack cannot be mistaken for a deletion-set signal.

forget_vs_unseen.description: Diagnostic only. High values here are consistent with either a deletion signal or a plain membership signal, so this task cannot separate the two hypotheses on its own.

forget_vs_rest.description: One-vs-rest form of the primary task, over the pooled negatives.

retain_vs_unseen.description: The third axis of the three-way problem. Reported with D_retain as the positive class, so a score that is lower for retained samples yields an AUC below 0.5 -- which for several scores is the predicted direction and is declared as such below.

forget_vs_rest.rationale: Pooled form of forget_vs_retain and forget_vs_unseen.

forget_vs_retain.rationale: ghat is dominated by the update that raised loss on D_forget. A forget sample's gradient at the unlearned parameters still carries a component along that displacement; a retain sample's contribution to ghat is the descent half of the update, averaged over a set several times larger, so its per-sample alignment is smaller.

forget_vs_unseen.rationale: As for forget_vs_retain, with an even larger expected gap.

member_vs_unseen.rationale: Both forget and retain samples participated in producing ghat; unseen data did not, so its alignment sits at the 1/d random-geometry floor.

retain_vs_unseen.rationale: Retained samples drove the gradient-descent half of the update, so they carry some alignment with ghat; unseen samples carry none.

forget_vs_retain.rationale: Both factors are declared higher-is-forget on this task.

forget_vs_unseen.rationale: Both factors are declared higher-is-forget on this task.

member_vs_unseen.rationale: The two factors pull in OPPOSITE directions here -- cos^2 is higher for members, SIF is lower -- so the product partially cancels. The declared direction follows cos^2, which spans several orders of magnitude and so dominates the log-space ranking. Near-chance is the expected outcome.

retain_vs_unseen.rationale: Follows cos^2 for the same dominance reason as member_vs_unseen; the SIF factor pulls the other way and partial cancellation is expected.

fuma_lora_ratio.label: FUMA-style LoRA / non-LoRA gradient magnitude ratio

forget_vs_retain.rationale: The premise the method rests on: data whose influence was manipulated through the adapters leaves a disproportionate share of its gradient on the adapter parameters relative to the backbone.

forget_vs_unseen.rationale: Follows forget_vs_retain.

member_vs_unseen.rationale: The adapters are where all task-specific fitting happened, so members of either kind should concentrate more gradient there than unseen data.

retain_vs_unseen.rationale: Follows member_vs_unseen.

forget_vs_retain.rationale: METHOD-DEPENDENT; the assumption is declared here rather than decided afterwards. Under GA+GD the ascent on D_forget is halted by a loss-ratio criterion, not by convergence, so forget samples end in a raised-loss region with large residual gradients while retain samples sit near a descent optimum. Under SCRUB the forget objective is -KL - entropy rather than +NLL, so the NLL gradient magnitude is not directly driven up and the same direction is assumed but expected to be weaker. If SCRUB lands below 0.5 that is reported below 0.5.

forget_vs_unseen.rationale: Follows the GA argument in forget_vs_retain.

member_vs_unseen.rationale: A fitted sample sits nearer a stationary point of its own loss, so its gradient is smaller. This is the classical gradient-norm membership signal.

retain_vs_unseen.rationale: Retained samples are fitted; unseen samples are not.

forget_vs_retain.rationale: The reference is the pre-unlearning fine-tuned model (LoRA mode) or the pretrained base (full fine-tuning mode); either way the ratio isolates the change unlearning made, so the GA argument for grad_norm_sq applies with the pre-existing per-sample scale divided out.

forget_vs_unseen.rationale: Follows forget_vs_retain.

member_vs_unseen.rationale: With the fine-tuned model as reference this largely cancels: the reference fitted the members too. Near-chance is the expected outcome and is reported as such.

retain_vs_unseen.rationale: Follows member_vs_unseen; expected near chance.

forget_vs_retain.rationale: Monotone transform of grad_ratio wherever both norms exceed eps, so the AUCs coincide there; it differs only in the underflow regime, where the additive eps keeps the score finite.

forget_vs_unseen.rationale: Monotone transform of grad_ratio.

member_vs_unseen.rationale: Monotone transform of grad_ratio.

retain_vs_unseen.rationale: Monotone transform of grad_ratio.

forget_vs_retain.rationale: Additive form of loss_ratio; same reasoning, same direction.

forget_vs_unseen.rationale: Additive form of loss_ratio; same reasoning, same direction.

member_vs_unseen.rationale: Additive form of loss_ratio; same reasoning, same direction.

retain_vs_unseen.rationale: Additive form of loss_ratio; same reasoning, same direction.

forget_vs_retain.rationale: Dividing by the base model's loss removes intrinsic sample difficulty, which is a nuisance variable here, not a signal. It does not change the direction of the unlearning effect.

forget_vs_unseen.rationale: As for loss_unlearned, with difficulty divided out.

member_vs_unseen.rationale: Calibrated membership signal; same direction as raw loss.

retain_vs_unseen.rationale: Calibrated membership signal; same direction as raw loss.

loss_unlearned.label: Raw loss under the unlearned model

forget_vs_rest.rationale: Follows forget_vs_retain, which supplies most of the negatives.

forget_vs_retain.rationale: Raising loss on D_forget while holding it down on D_retain is the objective of every unlearning method evaluated here, so this is the most direct consequence of the intervention.

forget_vs_unseen.rationale: ASSUMPTION, stated before measurement: gradient ascent overshoots, so the forget set ends above the never-trained baseline rather than merely returning to it. If unlearning only restores the baseline, the AUC lands at 0.5; that is a real result and is reported as such, not re-oriented.

member_vs_unseen.rationale: Standard loss-threshold MIA: fitting a sample lowers its loss. Note this is the OPPOSITE direction from forget_vs_retain, which is precisely why one loss threshold cannot serve both tasks.

retain_vs_unseen.rationale: Retained samples are still fitted members; membership lowers loss.

forget_vs_retain.rationale: DIRECTION RESTS ON A CONVENTION, hence headline: false. With ghat = theta_unlearned - theta_finetuned and gradient ascent on the forget set, the forget gradient at theta_unlearned points along the continued-ascent direction, i.e. positively along ghat. Under SCRUB the forget objective is -KL - entropy rather than +NLL and no such argument is available. Recorded for inspection; excluded from the comparison.

forget_vs_unseen.rationale: Same convention-dependent argument as above.

member_vs_unseen.rationale: Same convention-dependent argument as above.

retain_vs_unseen.rationale: Same convention-dependent argument as above.

forget_vs_retain.rationale: Self-influence measures how much the model's fit at z would move if z were reweighted. Unlearning removed the fit on D_forget, so those samples regain high self-influence while retained samples keep low self-influence.

forget_vs_unseen.rationale: Assumed, and weak: both classes are unfitted at this point, so the two may be indistinguishable. Near-chance is a real result here.

member_vs_unseen.rationale: Members were fitted and therefore have low self-influence. Under this declared direction the retain-vs-unseen AUC is expected BELOW 0.5 when read with retain as the positive class -- see retain_vs_unseen below.

retain_vs_unseen.rationale: Retained samples are fitted, so their self-influence is lower than that of unseen samples. Declared explicitly because the raw AUC with retain as positive will read below 0.5, and that is the predicted direction, not an absence of signal.

metadata.orientation_policy: AUCs use the preregistered direction for each (score, task). max(AUC, 1-AUC) is not used anywhere in this evaluation.

unlearning_direction.access: white-box: both the fine-tuned pre-unlearning checkpoint and the unlearned checkpoint are read directly
unlearning_direction.sign_note: cos^2 is sign-invariant, so this convention affects only raw_cosine, which is not a headline score

discrepancies: the exact published FUMA formula was not verifiable from this environment; the convention used here is stated explicitly (norm=l1_mean_abs, weighting=parameter) and is configurable -- see docs/FUMA.md
LoRA membership is decided by the substring 'lora' in the parameter name, matching PEFT's own naming

both the numerator and the denominator are taken from an unquantised bf16 copy of the unlearned model, not from the 4-bit model that was actually unlearned: bitsandbytes does not backpropagate into 4-bit weights, so the denominator does not exist on the scored model
the backbone is unfrozen purely to obtain gradients; it was frozen during training, so these gradients describe a direction the optimiser never took
the non-LoRA group includes the embedding and output projection, which dominate the parameter-weighted denominator

forget_vs_retain.rationale: Monotone transform of grad_ratio wherever both norms exceed eps, so the AUCs coincide there; it differs only in the underflow regime, where the additive eps keeps the score finite.

forget_vs_unseen.rationale: Monotone transform of grad_ratio.

retain_vs_unseen.rationale: Monotone transform of grad_ratio.

forget_vs_retain.rationale: Dividing by the base model's loss removes intrinsic sample difficulty, which is a nuisance variable here, not a signal. It does not change the direction of the unlearning effect.

forget_vs_unseen.rationale: As for loss_unlearned, with difficulty divided out.

member_vs_unseen.rationale: Calibrated membership signal; same direction as raw loss.

retain_vs_unseen.rationale: Calibrated membership signal; same direction as raw loss.

loss_unlearned.label: Raw loss under the unlearned model

forget_vs_rest.rationale: Follows forget_vs_retain, which supplies most of the negatives.

forget_vs_retain.rationale: Raising loss on D_forget while holding it down on D_retain is the objective of every unlearning method evaluated here, so this is the most direct consequence of the intervention.

forget_vs_unseen.rationale: ASSUMPTION, stated before measurement: gradient ascent overshoots, so the forget set ends above the never-trained baseline rather than merely returning to it. If unlearning only restores the baseline, the AUC lands at 0.5; that is a real result and is reported as such, not re-oriented.

member_vs_unseen.rationale: Standard loss-threshold MIA: fitting a sample lowers its loss. Note this is the OPPOSITE direction from forget_vs_retain, which is precisely why one loss threshold cannot serve both tasks.

retain_vs_unseen.rationale: Retained samples are still fitted members; membership lowers loss.

forget_vs_retain.rationale: DIRECTION RESTS ON A CONVENTION, hence headline: false. With ghat = theta_unlearned - theta_finetuned and gradient ascent on the forget set, the forget gradient at theta_unlearned points along the continued-ascent direction, i.e. positively along ghat. Under SCRUB the forget objective is -KL - entropy rather than +NLL and no such argument is available. Recorded for inspection; excluded from the comparison.

forget_vs_unseen.rationale: Same convention-dependent argument as above.

member_vs_unseen.rationale: Same convention-dependent argument as above.

retain_vs_unseen.rationale: Same convention-dependent argument as above.

forget_vs_retain.rationale: Self-influence measures how much the model's fit at z would move if z were reweighted. Unlearning removed the fit on D_forget, so those samples regain high self-influence while retained samples keep low self-influence.

forget_vs_unseen.rationale: Assumed, and weak: both classes are unfitted at this point, so the two may be indistinguishable. Near-chance is a real result here.

member_vs_unseen.rationale: Members were fitted and therefore have low self-influence. Under this declared direction the retain-vs-unseen AUC is expected BELOW 0.5 when read with retain as the positive class -- see retain_vs_unseen below.

retain_vs_unseen.rationale: Retained samples are fitted, so their self-influence is lower than that of unseen samples. Declared explicitly because the raw AUC with retain as positive will read below 0.5, and that is the predicted direction, not an absence of signal.
